item.title: Izu Peninsula: Hot Springs, Wild Coasts and a UNESCO Geopark — Guide
item.description: The Izu Peninsula juts into the Pacific south of Mount Fuji, formed over millions of years by volcanic islands colliding with Honshu, a geological origin so distinctive that the entire peninsula is designated a UNESCO Global Geopark. Its dramatic coastlines range from the rugged cliffs and sea caves of the west to white-sand beaches in the south, while inland valleys grow Japan’s finest wasabi, and celebrated onsen towns like Atami and Shuzenji have drawn bathers for centuries, all within a couple of hours of Tokyo.

item.title: Echizen Misaki Lighthouse: A Dramatic Cliffside Coastal Lighthouse — Guide
item.description: Echizen Misaki Lighthouse sits perched on rugged cliffs at the tip of the Echizen Peninsula, offering magnificent views of the open Sea of Japan and access to atmospheric coastal walking trails winding along the promontory. The austere beauty of this remote headland, considerably less visited than Fukui’s more famous Tojinbo Cliffs, makes it a good choice for travellers seeking solitude and dramatic seascape photography away from larger crowds. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Echizen, Fukui Hours Always accessible (exterior); lighthouse grounds daylight hours Admission Free Time needed 1–1.

item.title: Noto Peninsula: Rugged Coastlines and Rural Satoyama Landscapes — Guide
item.description: The Noto Peninsula juts into the Sea of Japan from Ishikawa’s northern coast, offering a considerably slower-paced counterpoint to Kanazawa’s city sights, with rugged coastal scenery, traditional fishing villages and terraced rice paddies that helped earn the region UNESCO recognition as a Globally Important Agricultural Heritage System for its traditional satoyama land management practices. The peninsula’s more remote, less-visited character rewards travellers with time to explore, offering an authentic look at rural coastal Japan increasingly rare elsewhere in the country.

item.title: Oarai Coast: A Torii Gate Rising From the Sea — Guide
item.description: Oarai Coast is home to one of Ibaraki’s most photographed and instantly recognisable scenes — the Kamiiso torii gate, standing on a rock formation just offshore from Isosaki Shrine, appearing to rise directly from the Pacific Ocean. The dramatic composition is especially striking at sunrise, when the gate is silhouetted against the colours of the rising sun over open water, drawing photographers and shrine visitors alike to this rugged stretch of coastline north of Tokyo.
